sections.h2: Picking a sale route in Newnan
sections.html:
Newnan is the Coweta County seat, roughly 35 miles southwest of Atlanta on Interstate 85. Owners here tend to weigh a listing against a private sale or an as-is cash purchase, and the answer usually follows the age of the house and how fast you need to be done. A cash purchase fits a house with deferred repairs, an inherited property or a hard deadline. A listing fits a house in good shape with time to spare.

Compare offers on price, closing date and recording costs, and name any liens, tenants or estate issues up front.

About 45,867 people live in Newnan by the mid-2025 estimate, 8.0 percent more than the 42,451 in the 2020 base. Of 17,180 households, 58.2 percent own their homes. The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $364,700, and median rent is $1,542. A bungalow near the square and a subdivision house out by the bypass will not match those averages, so look at what sold nearest to you.

Newnan's nickname is the "City of Homes," and antebellum and early 20th century houses survive in several historic districts. Cotton money and the railroad made it one of the richest towns per person in America by the mid 1800s, and the R.D. Cole company, which began as a sawmill in 1854, built most of the city's homes from the 1880s into the early 1900s. That explains the shared woodwork details buyers notice.

The city lists seven districts, and several are residential:

  • Cole Town grew around the Cole company and carries its woodwork.
  • College-Temple, laid out in 1828, has tree-lined streets, churches and a former academy lot.
  • Greenville-LaGrange covers 61 acres, with the oldest and grandest houses on the main streets.
  • Platinum Point is a 43-acre district of early 20th century houses north of town.
  • Newnan Cotton Mill and Mill Village includes a mill now converted to loft apartments.
  • Chalk Level, about 261 acres in southeast Newnan, joined the Georgia Register of Historic Places on October 24, 2025 and the National Register on January 29, 2026.

If your house is in one of them and exterior changes are planned, ask Planning and Zoning at 770-254-2354 whether design review applies.

The Building Department sits upstairs in City Hall at 25 LaGrange Street and takes permit applications on weekdays until 4:30 p.m. An application must include:

  • A site plan and a building plan
  • A ResChek or Comchek compliance report
  • Contractor licenses and a subcontractor list
  • The applicable fees

Records of past work help at sale time, because unrecorded additions tend to show up under a buyer's inspection.

Tree work has its own rule. A homeowner pays no fee to remove trees on a single-family lot until more than five come down at once in a calendar year, while anyone paid to cut trees needs a permit for each one eight inches across or larger. Specimen trees follow separate rules.

sections.h2: Coweta homestead and senior school tax exemptions
sections.html:
Coweta grants a basic homestead exemption to owners who live in the home on January 1, and its local senior school tax tiers carry no income limit. The 2026 amounts are:

Coweta senior school tax exemptions, 2026
CodeAge by January 1School tax exemption
LC65$75,000
LE71$100,000
LG75Full exemption

A homestead exemption stays with the person, so the buyer files a new application with the Assessors' Office. Each individual or married couple gets just one.

The Assessors' Office at 37 Perry Street sets values, and the Tax Commissioner at 87 Newnan Station Drive bills and collects. Assessment notices go out in early summer and open a 45-day appeal window, and each notice states its own deadline.

October brings the bills. One goes to the legal owner as of January 1 and another to the current owner on the Assessors' file, so a house sold after New Year's produces two. A parcel with an unresolved appeal gets a temporary bill set at 85 percent of the proposed value, and the final ruling produces a refund or an additional charge. Residential homestead bills for 2026 also carry the state's Homeowner Tax Relief Grant credit.

Homeowners with escrow should forward the bill to their servicer, because lenders often pay just weeks ahead of the deadline. Card payments add 2.5 percent (3 percent for American Express), and an online e-check costs $1.50. Call the Assessors at 770-254-2680 or the Tax Commissioner at 770-254-2670.

sections.h2: Clearing out a house before listing
sections.html:
Cleanout is simple in Newnan. Junk pickup needs no appointment: set items by the street on your regular collection day. Yard debris and bulk waste go through the Sanitation Department at 770-253-0327. Bagged trash must sit inside the cart, and the city will not take anything left beside it, although a second cart can be added. The AMWASTE service puts trash and recycling in one container.

Burning is allowed only with a permit from the Fire Marshal, reachable at 770-253-1851, extension 302. If a basement or outbuilding is full, start early so inspectors and buyers can see the structure.

sections.h2: From offer to closing in Newnan
sections.html:
1. Pull your deed, the latest Coweta bill and any permit records for past work.
  2. Check whether the house sits in a historic district before you promise exterior work.
  3. Ask the Tax Commissioner whether the house will produce two bills this year.
  4. Have the closing attorney set out in the contract who pays each bill and the transfer tax.
  5. Clear the house, since a buyer's inspector needs to see every room and outbuilding.

A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and most repair requests, so it moves faster when the house is dated or needs work. A listing reaches more buyers, but the lender sets the closing date.

sections.h2: Recording the deed in Coweta County
sections.html:
The Superior Court Clerk's Real Estate Division keeps every Coweta record and files documents daily in arrival order. Posted fees include $25 for a deed, $10 for a plat and $1 a page for copies, and personal checks are refused. The PT-61 transfer tax form must be e-filed with every title change. Self-filers need identity verification, while attorneys, lenders, title companies and brokers may file on paper.

Georgia's transfer tax, $1 per first $1,000 with 10 cents per further $100, shows on the settlement statement too. Owners can also sign up for free real estate fraud alerts through the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority. The closing attorney or title company typically files the deed after a Newnan closing.

faqs.q: Do I owe Coweta property tax after selling mid-year?
faqs.a: Possibly, because Coweta bills the January 1 owner of record and also mails a bill to the newest owner. Put the payment duty in the contract and settle it at closing.

faqs.q: When is the Newnan appeal deadline?
faqs.a: Each notice opens a 45-day window from its own date, and the deadline is printed on the notice. Call 770-254-2680 for help reading it.

faqs.q: Do Newnan's historic districts limit repairs?
faqs.a: They may. The city lists seven districts, including Cole Town, College-Temple, Downtown and Chalk Level. Call Planning and Zoning at 770-254-2354 before exterior work.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Coweta County?
faqs.a: The clerk lists $25 for a deed. Georgia's separate transfer tax is $1 for the first $1,000 of price plus 10 cents for each added $100 or fraction.

faqs.q: Who files the deed after a Newnan closing?
faqs.a: Typically the closing attorney or title company. Self-filers must e-file after identity verification.
